clue.text: Drink in bed in school

indicators.note: the second 'in' places the bed within the school abbreviation

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a drink in their dormitory bed at boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky from Scotland is called Scotch, a familiar drink.

clue.text: Ancient Greek female has pop disturbed

indicators.note: troubled or upset, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A woman of classical Greece is upset by modern pop music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was a celebrated lyric poet of ancient Lesbos, a Greek woman.

clue.text: Be more than relatively stupefied, unconscious at the start

indicators.note: placed at the beginning, so this piece leads the charade

parts.note: out cold means unconscious
comparative of numb, more stupefied

explanation.surface: Someone is more dazed than a relative, having been knocked out first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' signals a comparative: more numb gives NUMBER, read as a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber is to exceed in quantity, to be greater in count than.

clue.text: Study what sounds like marine mammal's hide

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal; the apostrophe s is a link

explanation.surface: Someone examines the pelt of a seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a noun meaning skin, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of sight, a synonym of hide.

clue.text: Bashing with a bit of power when stuck in grass

indicators.note: being stuck in something means lodged inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, to sing to the police
a watt is a unit of power

explanation.surface: Someone hits at something with a little force while it is caught in long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for informing to the police, and 'sing' is the same idea in criminal slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Swatting a fly means striking it hard, so bashing is a synonym.

clue.text: Put on paper as something deemed to have lost value

definitions.text: something deemed to have lost value
definitions.meaning: in accounting, an asset reduced in book value has been marked down

explanation.surface: An item recorded in writing is judged to have lost its worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded in writing is the plain sense; the accounting sense is an asset whose stated value is reduced.

clue.text: Airway with skill being set up, mostly inexpensive

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: art is skill

indicators.note: most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: cheap means inexpensive

explanation.surface: A cheap airline route is set up with expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being set up' reverses ART to TRA; 'mostly' drops the last letter of CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea, or windpipe, is the tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Bride always keeps so perfect

indicators.note: holds within, so the answer is contained inside these words

explanation.surface: A bride who always keeps things just right is flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something without fault, exactly as it should be.

clue.text: Assembled to be picked up

definitions.meaning: collected up, or understood, as in inferred

explanation.surface: Things were put together, ready to be collected.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: people come together, and items or flowers are collected up.

clue.text: Strong temporary accommodation established by river

indicators.note: set up beside, so the river comes before the tent in a charade

parts.note: the Po is the chief river of northern Italy
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: A sturdy camp shelter has been pitched beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A potent drink or argument is a powerful, forceful one.

clue.text: Fibre shown by female, one getting keen

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to keen is to wail in grief, to lament

explanation.surface: A thread is displayed by a woman who is enthusiastic about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager, but here it is the verb to wail for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A filament is a slender thread, such as a fine strand of fibre.

clue.text: Dishevelled hobo ate with us in home by bank maybe

indicators.note: untidy and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scruffy tramp shares a meal with us inside a dwelling near a river bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat used as a dwelling is moored, perhaps by a river bank, making it a waterside home.

clue.text: Attitude that is not heartless evident in speech

indicators.note: showing up inside, so these letters sit within the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: with its middle removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A speech plainly shows a stance that is far from callous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle letter of NOT to leave NT; IENT goes into ORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An orientation is one's stance or outlook, so it means an attitude.

clue.text: Orchestra in assembly room finishing with Beethoven's Third

indicators.note: ending with, so this letter comes last in the charade

parts.note: a large public room where people gather for meetings

indicators.note: the third letter of the composer's name is taken

explanation.surface: An orchestra plays in a meeting room, ending the concert with Beethoven's Third Symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hallé is a famous symphony orchestra based in Manchester.

clue.text: Nonsense talked in Brussels? Something perhaps at the breakfast table

definitions.meaning: waffle is empty verbose talk, and Brussels is the Belgian capital, so this is whimsical Belgian chatter

definitions.text: Something perhaps at the breakfast table
definitions.meaning: a thick grid-patterned batter cake of the Belgian style, eaten at breakfast

explanation.surface: Diplomats talk rubbish in Brussels while someone sits down to breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: British 'waffle' means rambling, pointless talk as well as the batter cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian-style batter cake is a breakfast dish, and the punning sense is rambling chatter from Belgium.

clue.text: Bat seen in one side of Oxford?

parts.note: one side, the first half, of this city's name is OXF, which is what the letters of fox give when sent flying into a new order

explanation.surface: A bat is spotted on one side of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: fox, with 'flying' as an anagram signal, gives OXF, the first half of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit bat of tropical regions is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: One may have a number of bowlers not being used

definitions.text: One may have a number of bowlers not being used

parts.words: One may have a number of bowlers not being used
parts.note: bowlers suggest cricketers resting, but they are bowler hats hung up when not worn

explanation.surface: A cricket captain keeps several bowlers idle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowlers seem to be cricketers left out of the attack; they are hard felt hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand in a hallway for hanging hats holds bowlers that are not being worn.

clue.text: Noisy clamour spreading out around India in bitter manner

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about the single letter
the letters disperse and settle into a new order

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A loud uproar spreads around the country of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading out' rearranges NOISY CLAMOUR, and 'around' puts that anagram about I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is bitterness, so acting with acrimony means behaving bitterly.

clue.text: Indicating ruler faced with ruin

indicators.note: confronted by, so the ruin piece stands in front

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch faces destruction, as the signs show.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking something means pointing it out or signalling it, like indicating.

clue.text: Jane, for one, certainly upset before lament's cut short

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: yes, certainly

indicators.note: shortened, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: to mourn is to lament; the apostrophe s stands for is

explanation.surface: Jane is surely distressed before her grief is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses YES to SEY; 'cut short' drops the N from MOURN. Jane Seymour was Henry VIII's third wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Seymour, the queen of Henry VIII, is an example of someone bearing this surname.

clue.text: Fights in beastly homes about nothing

indicators.note: surrounding, so the homes go round the nothing

parts.note: setts are badgers' burrows, the homes of beasts
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Fights break out in animal dens over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or argument, so the plural means scraps.

clue.text: Tease us about making money

indicators.note: turned about, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Someone mocks us over how to make cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is old slang for money, cash in hand.

clue.text: In short match the French shine

indicators.note: placed within, so the French article goes inside
cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a game is a match
le is French for the

explanation.surface: During a brief match, the French team shines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter of the match word before the article goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash of light, a synonym of a shine.

clue.text: A canny one turning into a nuisance

indicators.note: changing into something else, so these letters become a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shrewd person becomes a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: An annoyance is something irritating, a synonym of a nuisance.

clue.text: Drink? A fairy gets it knocked back, loudly

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth

indicators.note: drunk down, but read as sent backwards, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A fairy is offered a drink and downs it in one, noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suits the drinking surface but reverses IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Walk from house, love getting healthy

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
fit means in good health

explanation.surface: Leaving home on foot, a lover is getting into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoof it is informal for going on foot, to walk.

clue.text: Having bad effect on mother, a drink, little good

indicators.note: placed on, so the mother piece comes first and the rest follow it

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
gin is a spirit
G is the short form of good

explanation.surface: Drinking does harm to a mother who takes a gin, with little benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaging is harmful, having an injurious effect.

clue.text: Publicity provided by alliance for accepted custom

indicators.note: supplied alongside, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity work
the Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan

explanation.surface: Promoting a coalition's work becomes standard practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxis means established practice, the accepted way of doing something.
